input.description: Reframe the experiment so that chain/shortest-path supervision is an explicit prior-art control, not a claimed contribution (path-based reasoning over KG subgraphs is established: MHGRN unifies path-based reasoning, Variational Reasoning trains over latent KG paths). The inferential target becomes the residual: under a matched supervision token budget, identical templates, and identical test-time context, does chain + same-passage peripheral triples beat (a) chain-only supervision and (b) a chain + shuffled/unrelated-triple arm of equal length? Report Hits@1 by hop depth and a one-hop failure rate. The repair loop and RL stage are dropped from the primary contribution.
input.expected_benefit: Makes the surviving claim falsifiable and honest: chain supervision is credited to prior work, and the paper's result is either a measured (likely small) peripheral-context effect or a clean boundary/negative finding. The shuffled-context arm at matched budget directly tests the strongest counter-evidence (the +0.003 F1 inference-time result) on the training side, where it has not been tested.
input.experimental_difficulty_basis: Four matched-budget arms, byte-identical templates, multiple seeds, a hop-depth split with a construction check, and a format-controlled scorer; standard but careful, and the expected result in the peripheral arm may be null.
input.implementation_difficulty_basis: Reuses existing datasets (MetaQA/WebQSP/CWQ), an off-the-shelf 7B instruction model with LoRA, and existing KG/path construction; no new architecture and no RL infrastructure once the RL stage is dropped.
input.main_risk: If both the peripheral and shuffled arms are null, the result is purely negative; it must be pre-registered and framed as a boundary contribution, and a null chain effect would collapse the remaining premise entirely.
input.potential_novelty: Hedged and deliberately narrow: no retrieved work runs this matched-budget, inference-context-matched training ablation, so the comparison and the shuffled-context control are unoccupied. Because the chain component is prior art, novelty rests only on the peripheral-context boundary result and the hop-depth/one-hop-failure diagnostic, not on a new mechanism.

input.technical_mechanism: Construct four supervision views over the same targets (isolated triple/path; full reasoning chain; chain + same-passage peripheral triples; chain + shuffled unrelated triples) at matched token budget and with byte-identical instruction/output templates, fine-tune the same base model, and evaluate all arms under identical inference context, reporting per-hop Hits@1, one-hop failure rate, and a transfer gap.
input.title: Peripheral-context boundary test with chain supervision as a prior-art control
input.why_differs: Unlike MHGRN/Variational Reasoning (which establish path-based reasoning without a peripheral-context arm) and unlike the inference-time context systems (SG-RAG MOT, CLAUSE, Co-E), this isolates the training-time effect of peripheral context against a matched shuffled-context control with the chain credited to prior art; no retrieved work performs that contrast.

input.resolution: Largely resolved in the affirmative: the idea's effective component does reduce to established prior art. Supervision/inductive bias over the reasoning chain is already provided by path-based reasoning methods (MHGRN unifies path-based reasoning over KG subgraphs; Variational Reasoning learns multi-hop reasoning over latent KG paths), so 'expose the chain' is not a novel contribution. The repair loop additionally reduces to established process-supervision self-bootstrapping (KnowTrace) and generic iterative refinement (Self-Refine). What does not reduce is the residual question of whether peripheral (non-chain) same-passage triples contribute anything as training supervision - but the closest controlled evidence finds non-chain triples nearly inert at inference (+0.003 F1). So no novel contribution is demonstrated; the surviving claim is at most a boundary/negative result from one matched-budget training test, which is exactly what the revised modification M001 targets (G003).

input.description: The reduction of the chain arm to prior art depends on how prior path-based methods supervise: MHGRN uses a graph relation network over subgraphs and Variational Reasoning uses latent paths from QA pairs, whereas the revised idea would explicitly supervise an LLM with chain text. If explicit chain-text instruction supervision for multi-hop KGQA is already standard, even the chain arm is fully covered; if it is not, there is a modest implementation-level delta that should still not be presented as a mechanism contribution.
input.question: Is explicit reasoning-chain text supervision of an LLM for multi-hop KGQA already standard, or do prior path-based methods only use latent paths and graph modules?
input.rationale: This determines how much of even the chain arm is prior art and therefore whether any implementation-level residue can be claimed; the retrieved path-based works use latent or modular paths rather than explicit chain-text supervision, but coverage of this specific training format was not established.

input.direction: Reposition the work as a boundary test of the residual component rather than a method for context-enriched supervision. Chain/path supervision is credited to prior art and used only as a control; the repair loop and RL stage are dropped from the primary contribution. The deliverable becomes a matched-budget, inference-context-matched training comparison that asks whether peripheral same-passage context adds anything beyond the chain and beyond token budget, reported with per-hop accuracy, a one-hop failure rate, and a transfer gap - with a pre-registered negative/boundary outcome.
input.hypothesis: H1'': Under a matched supervision token budget, identical templates, and identical test-time context, adding peripheral same-passage triples to chain supervision yields no measurable multi-hop KGQA improvement over chain-only supervision, and performs no better than a chain + shuffled/unrelated-triple arm of equal length; any observed gain is attributable to the chain or to added tokens rather than to peripheral-context relevance. H2'': Per-hop failure attribution and a shallow-to-deep transfer gap can be measured reliably and localize whether multi-hop errors originate at the first hop.
input.rationale: U015 resolved largely in the affirmative: the effective ingredient (exposing the reasoning chain) is established path-based reasoning (MHGRN, Variational Reasoning), and the repair loop is established self-bootstrapping (KnowTrace, Self-Refine). What remains is not a method but a boundary question about peripheral context - untested at training time yet predicted near-inert at inference (+0.003 F1 for non-chain triples, with inflated context adding distractors). Continuing to ask 'does context-enriched supervision improve multi-hop KGQA' would overclaim prior art and conflate the chain effect with the peripheral effect; the original question is therefore replaced by the residual boundary test. This deserves investigation next because it is the only unoccupied and cheaply decidable question left in the idea, it directly tests the strongest counter-evidence on the training side where it has never been tested, and it yields a publishable boundary/negative result under pre-registration. The original idea and hypothesis remain recorded unchanged.
input.research_question: Under a matched supervision token budget and identical inference-time context, does training-time exposure to peripheral same-passage context triples add any measurable multi-hop KGQA accuracy beyond prior-art chain/path supervision and beyond a matched shuffled-triple control - and if not, can per-hop failure attribution and a shallow-to-deep transfer gap characterize where multi-hop errors originate?
